study.title: Criteria-gated Achilles rehab protocol: a progression template, no outcome data yet
study.evidence_note: Protocol only. Registry lists the trial as completed in 2023; no results paper found. A dosing and gating template, not evidence of benefit.
study.confidence_note: Free PDF read via summarising fetches; tables reconstructed, a few cells ambiguous. PMC blocked. Results search 2026-11-04 found none.
study.impact_line: A clear six-level template gating calf, hop and run loading on pain and strength targets. Untested: no results published.
key_findings: Protocol only: compares a 6-level criteria-based programme (SSC6) with Silbernagel pain-guided loading
Isometrics at Level 1 (5 x 45 s daily, calf-raise pain >5/10) and Level 6 maintenance
Gates: calf-raise pain <5 then <4/10; hop pain; <10% strength and RSI asymmetry
Calf load targets climb from >70% to >140% bodyweight added
Planned n=60 runners aged 18–45; primary outcome VISA-A change at 12 weeks
summary: Single-centre RCT protocol from the Sports Surgery Clinic, Dublin, in runners with MRI-confirmed mid-portion Achilles tendinopathy
SSC6 adds kinetic-chain strength, heavy calf loading, pogo hops, drop jumps and running drills
Comparator is Silbernagel's daily heel-raise programme, progressed by pain ≤4/10 with no strength targets
Barely addresses isometrics: entry rung for irritable tendons and heavy maintenance holds, not a tested intervention
No results reported; registry lists completion in May 2023
study.bottom_line: No outcome data, so it can't tell you whether criteria-gating beats pain-guided loading. Its value is a concrete, borrowable progression ladder that uses isometrics at entry and in maintenance.

key_numbers.label: Limb asymmetry gate, isokinetic strength and RSI

design: Registered NCT04384874, retrospectively (23 Apr 2020; recruiting from Jan 2020)
setting: Home or local gym; supervised session every 2–3 weeks
participants: MRI-confirmed mid-portion tendinopathy, 3 months to 3 years
Excludes injections in past 6 months, prior Achilles surgery, recent running injury
intervention: SSC6: enter at highest level whose criteria are met
L1 (wk 0–3, calf-raise pain >5/10): daily calf isometrics 5 x 45 s; box squat and step-up 3 x 8 at 10RM
L2 (pain <5/10): SL calf raise 4 x 8 at 10RM; seated SL calf raise 4 x 10 at 12RM; 3/wk
L3 (pain <4/10): same calf sets, targets >70% BW standing, >90% BW seated; ankling, marching, A-skips
L4 (10 double-leg hops <5/10, <10% isokinetic asymmetry): targets >80% and >110% BW; pogo hops 4 x 10
L5 (10 single-leg hops <4/10): eccentric SL raise >100% BW; drop jumps 4 x 4 from 20–30 cm; SL pogos 4 x 10
Exit L5: <10% asymmetry in single-leg vertical and horizontal RSI
L6 maintenance (wk 12–26): SL calf isometric 4 x 8 x 4 s holds >140% BW; drop jumps 4 x 5; SL pogos 4 x 12
Kinetic chain 2/wk throughout; loads raised weekly if pain doesn't rise
comparator: Phases 1–4: double, single, seated, eccentric then quick-rebound heel raises, 3 x 10–20
Weight added from phase 3 (amount not set); plyometrics as tolerated
Progress if pain ≤4/10 during and 24 h after
follow_up: Interviews at 6, 12 and 24 months; 6-month maintenance plan for both arms
methods.primary_outcome: Between-group difference in VISA-A change from baseline, mainly at 12 weeks

results.detail: Powered for a 15-point VISA-A difference, described as similar to previous studies, using a mean 12-week change of 21 (SD 6.6). Text lists 3, 6, 12 months; Table 3 lists 6, 12, 24 months.
Alpha 0.05, power 80%, 25 per group plus 15% dropout. A registry mirror lists the trial completed May 2023 with no results posted (last update Apr 2024).

results.result: Isokinetic plantar flexor torque, 3D running, drop jumps, hurdle hop stiffness
results.detail: Hop tests start at week 6. Diary records adherence, fidelity, NPRS and loads. Sport participation, re-injury and satisfaction asked at follow-up.

pico.p: Runners aged 18–45 with MRI-confirmed chronic mid-portion Achilles tendinopathy (3 months to 3 years)
pico.i: SSC6: six-level criteria-gated programme of kinetic-chain, calf, reactive strength and running drills
pico.c: Silbernagel pain-guided combined concentric-eccentric heel-raise programme
pico.o: VISA-A change at 12 weeks; strength, reactive strength and running/hopping biomechanics

limits: No outcome data: cannot support any effect claim
Retrospectively registered, three months after recruitment began
Intervention developed and funded by the trial clinic
Participants and treating clinicians unblinded; primary outcome self-reported
Results still unpublished about 3.5 years after registry completion

full_text.why: Read in full from the free full text (MMU repository PDF, CC BY); PMC was blocked by captcha. Tables reconstructed via summarising fetches; Level 1 split-squat row and the '60 s RM' isometric notation are ambiguous in the source.

how_to_apply: Don't change practice on this paper: it reports no outcomes.
Isometric entry dose: 5 x 45 s calf holds daily when single-leg calf-raise pain >5/10.
Set isometric load by tolerance; the protocol doesn't define its intensity.
Gate hopping on pain: 10 double-leg hops <5/10, then 10 single-leg hops <4/10.
Use <10% limb asymmetry in calf strength and RSI as objective progression checks.
Keep Silbernagel pain-monitoring (≤4/10, settled by 24 h) as the evidence-backed default.
applies_to: Runners with chronic mid-portion Achilles tendinopathy
Clinicians wanting explicit, measurable progression gates
Early-stage, irritable tendons needing an isometric starting rung
not_for: Claims that criteria-based rehab works better
Choosing isometrics over isotonics for pain relief
Over-45s or non-running populations without adaptation

grade.reason: Planned design has an unblinded self-reported primary outcome and retrospective registration.
Single trial, and no outcome data.
Planned population, intervention and outcome match the question for runners.
No outcome data: no estimate or CI. Powered at 80% for a 15-point VISA-A difference (n=60).
Registry shows completion May 2023, but no results found by Nov 2026.

clinical_significance: No effect estimate exists, so no MCID comparison or NNT is possible
Planned 15-point target exceeds the VISA-A MCID of about 6.5 points (McCormack 2015, inferred)
Study is powered only for a large difference; a smaller worthwhile one could be missed
comparator_fairness: Silbernagel is a credible, evidence-based comparator
Supervision matched: every 2–3 weeks in both arms
SSC6 adds kinetic-chain work and more exercise volume, so dose isn't matched
Comparator added weight isn't quantified, risking under-loading
alternative_explanations: Any future difference could reflect extra volume and novelty rather than criteria-gating
Expectation effects on self-reported VISA-A in an unblinded trial
Natural history and regression to the mean apply to both arms
spin: Protocol frames SSC6 as novel and multifactorial; no efficacy claims made
Silence on results since 2023 is itself a reporting concern
fit_with_evidence: Comparator mirrors Silbernagel 2007 pain-monitored loading, a standard of care
van der Vlist 2021 BJSM network meta-analysis found no clearly superior exercise type
No results published yet for NCT04384874 (registry: completed May 2023)
Fits the Atlas Achilles playbook as a progression option, not a new standard
external_validity: ✓ Home and gym-based, low supervision, like private practice
✗ MRI confirmation and isokinetic testing rarely available
✗ Single Irish sports clinic; older or sedentary patients excluded
would_change_my_mind: Published results showing a VISA-A difference beyond 6.5 points with a CI clearing it
A blinded-assessor replication with volume-matched arms
Evidence that a Level 1 isometric start improves early-stage outcomes
strengths: Blinded outcome tester for objective measures
Adherence and fidelity tracked by diary
Open access with full dosing tables
weaknesses: Arms not matched for exercise volume
appraisal.funding_conflicts: Internally funded by the Sports Surgery Clinic, which helped design the study and developed SSC6. Authors declared no competing interests.

verification.external_searched: PEDro title search on search.pedro.org.au: none (protocols not scored); site:pedro.org.au web search: none. No Cochrane or other review rating.

study.patient_explanation: This study planned to test whether moving through Achilles exercises using strength and hop targets works better than progressing by pain alone. Its results haven't been published, so it gives us a useful exercise ladder but no proof either way.
open_questions: Will results of NCT04384874 be published, and do they show a meaningful VISA-A difference?
Does an isometric-only first stage help irritable tendons more than early isotonic loading?
What isometric intensity does '60 s RM' mean in practice?
Can handheld dynamometry replace isokinetic testing for the 10% gate?

sources.citation: Griffin C, Daniels K, Hill C, et al. A criteria-based rehabilitation program for chronic mid-portion Achilles tendinopathy: study protocol for a randomised controlled trial. BMC Musculoskelet Disord 2021;22:695.
